messages:
Maria: quick dump — I ran a token-packing QoS sweep across the fleet (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). TL;DR: optimal max-tokens-per-batch is GPU-dependent, and KV-heavy workloads change the knee points a lot.

Ajay: nice. can you post the short table and the config you used?

Maria: pasted results below (condensed). each row = config applied to continuous-batching, 30m runs, mixed seq lengths, KV hit ratios at ~40% and ~80% buckets.

Maria: 
```
# packing sweep summary (tokens/sec = aggregate token throughput)
# columns: GPU | max_tokens_per_batch | p50_latency_ms | tokens_per_sec | pack_efficiency | notes
A10  | 8192  | 85  |  1800 | 0.72 | good balance, KV=40%
A10  | 16384 | 110 |  2050 | 0.61 | higher throughput but latency regresses on short seqs
T4   | 4096  | 95  |  700  | 0.68 | memory bound with KV=80%
T4   | 8192  | 150 |  820  | 0.45 | lots of fragmentation
L4   | 8192  | 60  | 1100  | 0.76 | sweet spot for L4 in FP16
L4   | 16384 | 95  | 1250  | 0.69 | diminishing returns
A100 | 32768 | 45  | 5200  | 0.84 | great throughput, KV cache warms well
A100 | 65536 | 70  | 5500  | 0.79 | memory pressure triggers suboptimal kernels
H100 | 65536 | 40  | 9000  | 0.88 | best for long sequences; supports larger pack sizes
H100 | 131072| 95  | 9200  | 0.72 | fragmentation and kernel fallback observed
```

Maria: pack_efficiency = packed_tokens / total_tokens_attempted. Lower when KV causes unusable slots.

Sam: interesting — did you record which kernel variants fired? (e.g., fused-attn vs fallback matmul loops)

Maria: yes. common pattern: when max_tokens_per_batch > GPU-specific memory headroom, kernel-selector flips from fused-attn (fast) to fallback matmul kernels that handle large seqs but cost latency. A100/H100 can stay on fused kernels longer. I captured a trace: `kernel_choice: fused_attn_v2 -> fallback_gemm` around OOM headroom boundary.

Liam: that explains the H100 knee at 131k — fallback triggers. Did you profile KV allocator fragmentation?

Maria: yes — KV allocations are per-request and we observed ~12% unusable fragmentation when seq-length variance > 4x. That means packer sees free slots that are unusable for new requests due to KV alignment.

Eva: was there a perf regression introduced somewhere? I remember a recent kernel-selector heuristic change last week.

Maria: yup. I re-ran with the pre-change image and saw ~7–12% better p50 on A10/A100 for medium pack sizes. The recent change raised the threshold to prefer quantized kernels; that interacts badly with PackHeadroom heuristics.

Ajay: any quick mitigation for the rollout? We need something safe for Dedicated clusters.

Sam: options: 1) set conservative per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch (use Maria's table), 2) enforce packer headroom percentage (e.g., reserve 12% for KV alignment), 3) tweak kernel-selector fallback thresholds to prefer fused_attn up to slightly higher memory usage.

Liam: also consider queue policy: prefer homogeneous batches by sequence length for long-seq lanes. That reduces fragmentation and keeps fused kernels usable. Could add one fast-path queue for long seqs on H100/A100.

Maria: experiment config I propose to A/B this week:
```
continuous_batching:
  per_gpu:
    A10: { max_tokens: 16384, reserve_headroom_pct: 12 }
    T4:  { max_tokens: 8192,  reserve_headroom_pct: 15 }
    L4:  { max_tokens: 16384, reserve_headroom_pct: 10 }
    A100:{ max_tokens: 65536, reserve_headroom_pct: 8 }
    H100:{ max_tokens: 131072, reserve_headroom_pct: 6 }
  queue_policies:
    - name: "long-seq-lane"
      seq_len_min: 8192
      prefer_gpu: [A100,H100]
    - name: "packed-default"
      seq_len_max: 8192
      pack_timeout_ms: 30
```

Eva: quick comment — lower pack_timeout for small seqs improved p50 in my microbenchmarks. 30ms seems fine.

Ajay: any impact on autoscaler/latency SLOs? If we increase reserve headroom, throughput per-GPU may drop, affecting cost targets. Need to model cost delta.

Maria: estimate: reserving 10–12% headroom reduces tokens/sec ~4–7% on A100/H100 but avoids kernel fallbacks that add p50 regressions up to 30% in worst cases. Net: better QoS, small cost increase. I'll run cost sims.

Sam: also flag for eng-sre: if we change per-GPU defaults, need to surface in Console per-route recommended settings and in rollout automation.

Liam: follow-ups:
- Maria -> run longer 4h runs with KV hit at 80% and 20% to confirm stability (owner: Maria)
- Sam -> add kernel-selector telemetry to batch traces (owner: Sam)
- Ajay -> cost modelling for Dedicated pricing impact (owner: Ajay)
- Eva -> microbench validating pack_timeout tweaks on L4/T4 (owner: Eva)

DeployBot: deploy request queued for canary with per_gpu overrides: A10/T4/L4 on canary1, A100/H100 on canary2. Will post results when finished. :rocket:

Maria: cool — I'll upload full traces + perf flamegraphs to the eng-runtime drive and link here once ready.

Ajay: thanks, this is actionable. let's avoid broad kernel-selector change until we A/B these per-gpu configs. :+1:

Maria: +1. I'll ping again with raw traces.
